title: Adaptive Early-Learning Correction for Segmentation from Noisy Annotations (ADELE)
note: Variant oof_add (confident unlabelled crack components set to crack, from N0 teacher dumps), offline. Runs only if gate G2 passes (ridge share >=50% in >=20 cells). Online ADELE was dropped in WAVE2_REVIEW (same pixels, leaky model, 6 build h). Same paper as arxiv:2110.03740 in T3.tsv.

title: Modeling annotator preference and stochastic annotation error for medical image segmentation (PADL)
note: Source-conditional prediction (one head per source plus consensus, source head at test) is on BRIEF section 5 never-tried list. No T3 arm covers it: matched_crack_head fixes placement, oof_soft_distill and oof_selective_ignore fix missing segments, none models per-source width or style, the only named route to strict crack IoU above 0.5. No code found, so build cost is real (about one 1x1 head per source). Check first that the source is known for every cell at test.

title: PNT-Edge: Towards Robust Edge Detection with Noisy Labels by Learning Pixel-level Noise Transitions
note: Variant: learned smooth warp module (max shift 3 px) in place of one-to-one matching. Run only if matched_crack_head passes and its tau_d=0 control shows alignment is credited. Placement noise here is random per point, not a smooth field, so the warp may absorb little. Code exists.

title: Learning robust medical image segmentation from multi-source annotations (UMA-Net)
note: Source routing to quality-specific heads is covered by the PROMOTE candidate P059 (per-source heads), which has the stronger mechanism match. No code found. Evidence is simulated lung data only.

title: Unlocking Robust Semantic Segmentation Performance via Label-only Elastic Deformations against Implicit Label Noise (NSegment+)
note: Label-only random elastic jitter of 0.5 to 1.5 px on crack and inactive labels, one dataloader change, about 11 GPU-h screen. Not covered: offset-tolerant CE (BRIEF section 5, n.d.) is a loss tolerance, this is a stochastic label regulariser; matched_crack_head changes the target by matching, not by resampling. Needs a card that handles the paper's small-segment exemption (inverted for cracks) and compares at matched width.

title: Noisy Supervision for Correcting Misaligned Cadaster Maps Without Perfect Ground Truth Data
note: Learned displacement-field label corrector; same mechanism as P319 (DragOSM), which has code, and ridge_snap_labels (merged with T4 ridge_snap) already tests label alignment with a cheaper offline snap. Numbers not read, no code. Revive only through P319.

title: From noisy labels to intrinsic structure: A geometric-structural dual-guided framework for noise-robust medical image segmentation (GSD-Net)
note: Most recent noise-robust baseline with public code (ortonwang/GSD-Net); belongs in the benchmark method suite for the label-noise stress track. Distance-weight idea is weaker than matched_crack_head for 1 to 2 px labels.

title: Imbalanced Medical Image Segmentation With Pixel-Dependent Noisy Labels (CLCS)
note: Noise-robust baseline for imbalanced classes with public code (Erjian96/CLCS); fits the benchmark suite. Its cleanliness voting acts on the same pixels as oof_selective_ignore, so no separate arm.

title: DragOSM: Extract Building Roofs and Footprints from Aerial Images by Aligning Historical Labels
note: Variant: learned label snapper trained on synthetic perturbed crack labels, replacing the profile-based ridge snap. Run only if the merged ridge_snap passes its pair check and screen (so alignment is shown to matter). Code exists (likaiucas/DragOSM). Also covers P254.

title: AIO2: Online Correction of Object Labels for Deep Learning With Incomplete Annotation in Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
note: Adds teacher-predicted components to labels, the same pixels as oof_add (offline variant of oof_selective_ignore, via P010). Online trigger and 2x FLOPs; evidence in NSegment+ comparison is +0.2 to +0.5 mIoU. Revive only if oof_add passes and an online version is wanted.

title: Object Detection as a Positive-Unlabeled Problem
note: nnPU risk inside the ridge mask tests missing-label tolerance, which oof_selective_ignore (F2) and oof_add already test with a leak-free teacher. Evidence is detection, not segmentation. Revive if G2 shows missing cracks are real but the add and ignore variants disagree.

title: A Bayesian Approach to Segmentation with Noisy Labels via Spatially Correlated Distributions
note: Variational latent-field model; covers jitter and omission, which oof_soft_distill and matched_crack_head already target with far less code. Abstract-level evidence only, extra variational training cost.

title: Prompt and Refinement: Asymmetric Mutual Learning for Infrared Small Target Detection with Noisy Labels
note: Unverified beyond an abstract fragment, no code. oof_soft_distill covers label correction from other models; mutual learning at 5% labels was already run (CPS, BRIEF section 5), not on the labelled set though.

title: Distribution-aware Noisy-label Crack Segmentation
note: SAM adapter fine-tuning belongs to the foundation-encoder family (BRIEF section 5 lists adapters and SAM fine-tuning as open); pavement crack data, no code. A named alternative there tests the same adapter mechanism.

title: SegFix: Model-Agnostic Boundary Refinement for Segmentation
note: Direction-map refinement needs an interior; useless for 1 to 2 px cracks. Only for blob classes (inactive, ribbons), where it is a post-processing stage, not a label-noise arm. No code found. Revive if a refinement stage for band classes is wanted.

title: IUR-Net: A Multi-Stage Framework for Label Refinement Tasks in Noisy Remote Sensing Samples
note: Abstract-level only, no code, remote sensing. Structural-class label cleaning is not the bottleneck; crack labels are, and ridge_snap and oof arms cover those.

title: Noisy Annotations in Semantic Segmentation
note: Spatial label-noise benchmark protocol (boundary distortion, class confusion). Use it to design the benchmark's label-noise stress track with calibrated crack jitter and source-width noise. Code available.
